purpose: Correct the chronology characterization of DCP-LETT-3428 and DCP-LETT-3429 without overwriting the earlier additive report.

corrections.corrected_date_assessment: The XML constraint is only [before 15 February 1862], with no supported lower bound, so it does not by itself exclude 1844–46. The editorial relationship and the specific Mormodes/Crocker episode place the record in the 1862 correspondence sequence; retain that as likely-era evidence rather than an XML-proven exclusion.

quote.text: Will you give me Mr W. C. Crockers (is this spelt right?) address in enclosed envelope: I am half mad about Mormodes perhaps he may know.

corrections.corrected_date_assessment: The XML constraint is likewise only [before 15 February 1862], with no supported lower bound. Its explicit reference to seeing Darwin at Lubbock’s on the coming Saturday, and editorial footnote 3 identifying that lunch as 15 February 1862, strongly supports the 1862 era; this is a supported editorial-era inference, not a lower-bound fact encoded by XML.

quotes.text: I doubt if he can help you with Mormodes What is it you want to know
I am to see you at Lubbocks on Saturday.
The reference is to the lunch at John and Ellen Frances Lubbock’s on 15 February 1862

link_correction.assessment: The direct address/Mormodes exchange remains supported, but its 1862-era placement rests on the editorial relationship and internal Lubbock reference, while the raw XML remains broadly bounded before 15 February 1862. Do not call these records simply pre-period or XML-proven outside 1844–46.
